title: Johan Zobel (Danish resident in Paris) → Christian IV: separate two-page sheet with nineteen words in a number cipher and letter code names, no decipherment
correspondents: Johan Zobel → Christian IV of Denmark
shelfmark: Rigsarkivet (Copenhagen), Tyske Kancelli, Udenrigske Afdeling (TKUA), Speciel del, Frankrig: Gesandtskabsrelationer, B.31: 1627-31, Gesandtskabsrelationer med bilag fra Johan Zobel
folio_note: Arkivalieronline epid 19852643, unit 261292 (366 images); image 241 right-hand page and image 242 left-hand page: one bifolium, about 21 + 17 lines of German with 19 cipher words (8 + 11), roughly 140 numbers; address and two seals on the outside. Pencil date '1629 20/9' at the foot of 241.
status: Viewed 11 Nov 2026 at full size (both pages). German in Zobel's hand with words replaced by runs of numbers 4-27 separated by full stops; each run starts with a number from 28 to 39 followed by a comma (e.g. '28, 24.4.9.9.8.16', '31, 13.11.14.9.23.25', '36, 14.12.16.19.25', and the same run again after 35). Persons and states are single code letters in the clear text (D., H., G., B., Bp., Bo.). Nothing is written over or beside the numbers, and no decipherment sheet lies next to it (images 234-250 viewed). It is the only cipher seen in the unit: images 1-366 were all viewed except 82-161 and 295-365, which were seen 1 in 4. Not on DECODE; Fridericia (1876) used the neighbouring letters of 16, 18 and 19 Sept 1629 but does not cite this one.
why: Zobel's confidential report to Christian IV four months after the peace of Lübeck, in the weeks when he was being displaced in Paris by Peder Vibe; the hidden words name what 'H.' and 'G.' are doing.
score_note: Scored from the scan during the third TKUA paging pass of 11 Nov 2026 (research/sweep_2026-11-11_tkua_paging_3/); both pages at full size
verify: Transcribe the 19 runs and solve as a simple substitution on 4-27 (the leading 28-39 looks like a null or an index: the same run follows 35 and 36). Identify D., H., G., B., Bp., Bo. from the clear letters of 16-19 Sept 1629 (images 231-240).

Words are replaced by runs of numbers 4-27 with full stops between them, each run headed by a number 28-39 and a comma; code letters D., H., G., B., Bp., Bo. stand for names. title: Johann Schultetus (Danish resident at The Hague) → Christian IV: reports of 1628-29 with code numbers, capital-letter cipher words and signs, no decipherment
correspondents: Johann Schultetus → Christian IV of Denmark; one French letter to an unnamed minister ('Monsieur')
shelfmark: Rigsarkivet (Copenhagen), Tyske Kancelli, Udenrigske Afdeling (TKUA), Speciel del, Nederlandene: B.41, 1608-34, Gesandtskabsrelationer, indberetninger og breve fra forskellige; inner folder 'Indberetninger, hvoraf enkelte med Bilag, fra Resident Johan Schultetus til Kong Christian IV, 1628-29'
folio_note: Arkivalieronline epid 19852699 (Daisy 11841122), unit 261377 (475 images); Schultetus's folder is images 426-475. Cipher seen at full size on 435 right (30 Sep 1628, one page, about 25 code groups), 451 (both pages, 9/19 Jan 1629, a long relation with a code group in most lines), 460 right ('Duplicata', 6 Mar 1629, about 30 groups), 461 right (French, 7 Mar 1629, about 45 numbers). The same hand and layout on 450, 452-456, 462-463, 471-473 (seen at 533 px, numbers visible) and probably 427-447 (seen at 400 px only).
status: Viewed 11 Nov 2026: unit sampled 1 image in 4, images 425-475 every image, six frames at full size. German letters in which names and key words are replaced by (a) numbers 12-596 standing alone (212, 319, 330, 381 for the place of writing, 425, 430, 431, 502, 503, 519, 565 ...), (b) words spelled in capital letters by a letter substitution (CVPRYTAAT, DCTNSL, NVCXLMP, FTMKPOPPTA, TZKTCPETE, EOPPTM, PRYVMTM, FZPNLC), and (c) signs (a heart for the king, a gamma-like sign, a figure-8 sign). The French letter of 7 Mar 1629 uses another system: runs of two-digit numbers with full stops (20.53.51.37.40.63.18.37.19.60; 64.65.51.71; 67.65.64.75.19.51) and three-digit codes (965, 836, 547, 628). No decipherment between the lines, in the margin or on a separate leaf on any frame viewed. Not on DECODE. Opel (1894) cites the letters without printing them.
why: The Danish resident's reports from The Hague in the last months of Christian IV's war with the Emperor (relief of Glückstadt and Krempe, Dutch and English subsidies, Morgan's troops, the Lübeck peace talks); the capital-letter words are a short route into the code.

Compare with the letters of Vosbergen and Brandt 1627-28 in the same unit (images 249-425) for the same numbers.

title: Peder Charisius (Danish resident at The Hague) → a minister ('Monsieur'): one-page German letter with eleven passages in signs and numbers, no decipherment
correspondents: Peder Charisius → an unnamed minister in Copenhagen ('Monsieur')
shelfmark: Rigsarkivet (Copenhagen), Tyske Kancelli, Udenrigske Afdeling (TKUA), Speciel del, Nederlandene: B.44, 1646-59, Gesandtskabsrelationer, til dels med bilag, fra Martin Tancke, Peter Christian Roch, Peder Charisius, Henrik Villumsen Rosenvinge og M. Rømer; inner folder 'Relationer fra Resident Peder Charisius 1655'
folio_note: Arkivalieronline epid 19852699, unit 261381 (633 images), image 441 right-hand page: 27 lines, about 95 cipher tokens in eleven passages. Images 442-443 are a copy of the Dutch States-General cipher (key lead); image 444 right is a German letter to 'Herr Resident' in a number cipher, deciphered between the lines.
status: Viewed 11 Nov 2026 at full size. German letter headed 'Monsieur', dated ''s Gravenhag 7 Junij', signed P. Charisius. Passages in a mixed cipher: signs separated by commas (a lambda-like sign, a gamma-like sign, a barred H, y, o, q, d, a cross, a doubled-bar sign) and numbers (10, 14, 25, 42, 50, 61, 103, 124, 128, 144, 145, 183, 202, 235, 272, 283, with 2a and 6a). Nothing over the lines or in the margin. The letter speaks of the 'equipage' made in England and what the Dutch government has resolved 'extraordinari'. The unit was sampled 1 image in 4 (1-633) and images 400-480 every image; this is the only undeciphered cipher seen in it.
why: Charisius's private word to Copenhagen in June 1655 on Dutch naval measures and England, in the months before the Swedish attack on Poland.
score_note: Scored from the scan during the third TKUA paging pass of 11 Nov 2026 (research/sweep_2026-11-11_tkua_paging_3/); the leaf at full size
verify: A probable deciphered sibling: Paul Klingenberg's embassy journal of 1665-67 (TKUA Nederlandene, Klingenbergs m.fl.s gesandtskabsarkiv, Journal A; Arkivalieronline epid 23897977, unit 673416, image 433 = pp. 852-853, colour scan) copies passages in a cipher of the same look (cross, double-cross, barred and lambda-like signs, d, q, y, with numbers 10, 14, 42, 109, 134) and gives their meaning in the margin under letters a, b, c ('zur continuation ... Monats subsidien fuer die Lueneb. troupen'). Whether it is the same key as the 1655 letter is not tested. Transcribe the leaf (about 95 tokens). The signs look like a letter alphabet and the numbers like syllables or names; look for the same cipher in Charisius's relations of 1656-60 (unit 261383) and in Peder Vibe's letters to Charisius ('Holland C', cited by Fridericia), where a deciphered sibling may lie.

title: Christian Pentz (Danish envoy in Vienna) → Christian IV: private letter with seventeen lines of a two-digit number cipher, no decipherment
correspondents: Christian Pentz → Christian IV of Denmark
shelfmark: Rigsarkivet (Copenhagen), Tyske Kancelli, Udenrigske Afdeling (TKUA), Speciel del, Tyskland, Kejseren: B. Gesandtskabsrelationer med bilag 1630-58; inner folder 'Relationer fra Grev Christian Pentz og Gotlieb v. Hagen 1636'
folio_note: Arkivalieronline epid 19852211 (Daisy 11623887), unit 260651 (534 images), images 36 right, 37 (both pages) and 38 left: a four-page autograph letter; cipher on 37 right (fourteen lines) and 38 left (three lines), about 170 numbers. The archive's pencil date '1636 26/3 5/4' is at the foot of image 36.
status: Viewed 11 Nov 2026 at full size (images 36, 37, 38). German in Pentz's own hand, signed 'Christian Pentz', dated 'Wien den 26 Martij / 5 Aprilis Ao 1636'. Numbers 8-64 written singly with spaces, some runs ended by a full stop, with larger numbers that look like code words (85, 165, 168, 226). Clear words stand between the runs ('betreffend habe ich', 'nicht allein', 'besondern'). Nothing is written above or beside the numbers. The same unit holds Sehested's Vienna letters of 1657 (images 108-172, a different cipher, catalogued) and the Frankfurt relations of 1657-58 (images 333-533), whose two-digit cipher is deciphered between the lines (357, 381 checked at full size). The unit was sampled 1 image in 4, images 30-44 every image.
why: Pentz's own report, apart from the joint relation with Hagen of the same day, on the Emperor's answer to Christian IV's offer of mediation with Sweden and on the Bremen succession (March 1636).
score_note: Scored from the scan during the third TKUA paging pass of 11 Nov 2026 (research/sweep_2026-11-11_tkua_paging_3/); the three frames at full size
verify: Transcribe the 170 numbers; the range 8-64 with repeats (33, 29, 17, 21, 22 are frequent) suggests a homophonic or simple letter substitution in German with a few code numbers (168 = a person, 226). Page the rest of the 1636 folder (images 33-100) at full size for more cipher and for a deciphered sibling.
